evals.prompt: Use scope-it for this settled discussion. The repository worktree is clean and there is no existing Baseline Pointer.
evals.expected_output: The agent completes the existing spec-and-ticket workflow without creating a branch, commit, push, or Baseline Pointer because there are no Scope-related Changes.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for this settled discussion. Two whole-file planning documents created during the discussion are the only worktree changes.
evals.expected_output: After selecting the Planning Owner Ticket, the agent creates an issue-linked branch from the latest remote default branch, commits only the two confirmed files, pushes and verifies the full SHA, returns the originating worktree to its entry branch, and posts exactly one fixed-format Baseline Pointer.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for this settled discussion. One changed file mixes this scope's ADR edits with unrelated draft notes.
evals.expected_output: The agent preserves the completed tracker artifacts but stops before branch creation because a changed file mixes scopes; it does not split hunks, commit, push, or publish a Baseline Pointer.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it after interruption. The linked baseline branch and commit already exist remotely, but the Planning Owner Ticket has no Baseline Pointer.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies and reuses the existing branch and commit, publishes only the missing pointer comment, creates no duplicate branch or commit, and reports the completed baseline artifacts.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for a settled design that genuinely needs three delivery tickets and has shared planning-document changes.
evals.expected_output: During the existing multi-ticket approval, the agent selects the unique ticket that owns the documents or the foundation ticket as Planning Owner Ticket; if no unique owner exists it asks there, then creates one shared baseline and publishes the same owner, branch, and full SHA pointer to every related ticket.

evals.prompt: A different agent resumes scope-it after interruption immediately after the Planning Baseline branch was checked out. The current branch is the baseline branch, and the previous agent wrote the original worktree, entry branch, and pinned remote-base SHA to repo-local Git config.
evals.expected_output: After selecting the Planning Owner Ticket, the new agent reads the exact scope-it.planning-baseline-<owner-number> keys, rejects a partial or malformed set, reuses the complete persisted entry and base metadata rather than recording the baseline branch as entry, and releases the original worktree before Baseline Pointer publication.

evals.prompt: Run scope-it until just before its first Planning Baseline branch checkout. The Planning Owner Ticket, original worktree and branch, and fetched 40-character remote-base SHA are known.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes entry-worktree, entry-branch, and base-sha under the fixed repo-local scope-it.planning-baseline-<owner-number> namespace, reads all three values back successfully, and only then checks out or creates the baseline branch.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it from a ready delivery issue whose native parent is a stable settled spec. The starting issue is one of several already-published sub-issue tickets, matches the current scope, and has no Scope-related Changes, Baseline Pointer, or linked planning branch.
evals.expected_output: The agent audits the native tracker relationship, reuses the parent spec and starting child ticket, selects the child as the delivery ticket, and reports Planning Baseline none without resolving or rerunning to-spec or to-tickets or creating duplicate tracker artifacts.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it after three approved delivery tickets were published from a tracker-backed spec issue. Every ticket body contains the correct Parent reference and the approved native blocking edges exist, but the spec issue has no native sub-issues even though the tracker supports them.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the Tickets checkpoint as incomplete because textual Parent references are not native containment evidence, adds only the exact missing sub-issue relationships to the three existing tickets without rerunning ticket analysis, reads back the complete child list, and does not begin Planning Baseline until containment is verified.
assertions: Treats the textual Parent references as insufficient native containment evidence and keeps Tickets incomplete.
Adds only the three missing native sub-issue relationships to the existing tickets without rerunning ticket analysis or creating issues.
Re-reads the Scope Parent's child list, preserves all issue content and metadata, and does not begin Planning Baseline before verification succeeds.

evals.prompt: Resume scope-it after all approved delivery tickets are verified native sub-issues of the spec issue, but one approved blocking edge is absent from the tracker.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats containment and dependency as independent evidence, adds only the missing blocking edge without rerunning ticket analysis or duplicating tickets or relationships, verifies the complete graph, and does not begin Planning Baseline before that verification succeeds.
assertions: Treats complete native containment as separate from the incomplete blocking graph.
Adds only the approved missing blocking edge while reusing every issue and pre-existing relationship.
Re-reads the blocking graph and does not begin Planning Baseline before verification succeeds.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it for an approved backend and frontend ticket split whose tracker supports cross-repository native sub-issues. The backend foundation ticket blocks the frontend ticket and uniquely owns the shared planning document.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies both delivery tickets as native sub-issues of the spec issue across repositories, independently verifies the backend-to-frontend blocking edge, then selects the backend ticket as Planning Owner without changing the Scope Parent or containment graph.
assertions: Verifies both backend and cross-repository frontend tickets as native sub-issues of the spec issue.
Independently verifies that the backend foundation ticket blocks the frontend ticket.
Selects the backend ticket as Planning Owner without changing the Scope Parent or containment graph.
